SpaceX has just leveled up with the Raptor 3 — easily the most advanced rocket engine on the planet right now.

It delivers roughly 280 tons of thrust (about 1.5x what the original Raptor 1 could do), costs around a quarter as much to build, and is significantly lighter. Those weight savings alone add up to roughly 43 tons less per Starship launch. 

Best part? No heat shield required anymore thanks to its cleaner, simplified design with internal controls and fewer parts.

The first flight with these beasts is eyed for Starship Version 3 this April.

Video

RAPTOR 3: THE MOST ADVANCED ROCKET ENGINE EVER BUILT

SpaceX just unveiled the next evolution of its Raptor engine family — and Raptor 3 is a massive leap forward.

This is the engine that will power Starship V3 and V4, pushing us closer to the rapid reusability and high-cadence launches needed for the Moon and Mars.

Why Raptor 3 is a game-changer:
•  Fully integrated regenerative cooling — The entire engine is cooled internally. No external heat shield required. This dramatically simplifies the design, reduces weight, and improves reliability.
•  Record thrust-to-weight ratio — Higher chamber pressure and optimized performance deliver more thrust per pound of engine mass than any previous version.
•  Fewer parts, easier to manufacture — Simplified architecture with integrated plumbing and fewer joints means faster production at scale and fewer potential failure points.
•  Insane power on liftoff — A full Starship stack with Raptor 3 engines will generate over 100 gigawatts of power at liftoff — roughly 20% of the entire U.S. electrical grid output — while staying intact and reusable.

Elon Musk on Raptor 3:

“Raptor 3 engine is a very advanced engine, by far the best rocket engine ever made. On liftoff, Starship is generating over 100 gigawatts of power. It’s 20% of US, while not exploding. There’s thousands of ways it could explode and only one way that it doesn’t.”

Raptor 3 is the heart of the most powerful and reusable launch system in history. Every improvement brings us closer to airline-like launch cadence and the tonnage needed to build a self-sustaining city on Mars.
The future of spaceflight runs on Raptor.

Video

STARSHIP FLIGHT 12 IS JUST 4–6 WEEKS AWAY — AND IT’S THE BIGGEST UPGRADE YET

This is going to be the most powerful version of Starship ever flown: the first full flight of the upgraded Version 3 (V3) ship and booster.

V3 brings:

•  More Raptors
•  Significantly more thrust and power
•  Bigger capabilities across the board
SpaceX is clearly pushing hard toward the next major milestones: rapid reusability, reliable orbital refueling, and the eventual Mars flights.
Every version gets noticeably better, and V3 looks like a serious leap forward.
The countdown is on. This one is going to be special.
